subject: Customer request: EU-only model tether + no-fallback — operational playbook
messages:
From: Olivia Mendes <olivia.mendes@nexahealth.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: EU-only model tether + no-fallback (security requirement)

Diego,

Thanks for taking this — we had a call with security and product yesterday and NexaHealth has a hard requirement for the pilot: all inference for PHI flows must remain in EU regions, and for a small set of endpoints they require a no-fallback policy (i.e., requests must not be routed to alternate model variants or non-EU infra). They also want the production deployment to be pinned to a specific model variant (we referenced "redwood-llm-v2-priv-quant" in the call).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can support:
- EU-only routing enforcements for specific routes
- an operational no-fallback (hard lock) for those routes
- forced model selection (pin to variant) with token accounting and SLA implications documented

I've attached the security questionnaire they asked us to fill as part of procurement. If you need a follow-up call with their InfoSec, include Tom (cc).

Olivia
Customer Success Manager
NexaHealth

Attachment: NexaHealth_Security_Questionnaire.pdf
From: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: evelyn_hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-18T10:01:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: EU-only model tether + no-fallback (security requirement)

Forwarding Nexa's ask — key asks are EU-only routing for certain endpoints, an enforced no-fallback policy for that traffic, and pinning to a specific model variant. They flagged PHI so procurement is moving fast.

Questions for product/ops:
- Feasibility: can we implement a per-route "no-fallback" flag that prevents any runtime reroute to other variants/regions?
- Risk: what are the run-time failure modes (GPU OOMs, kernel regressions, quantization mismatch) and how do we guarantee continuity?
- SLA/Work: rough estimate of engineering + infra changes and any changes to support docs/playbooks.

If we can do this, we'll need a short ops playbook (deployment checklist, rollback steps, monitoring alerts) and legal to sign the contract amendment (DocuSign).

Diego
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-18T11:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: EU-only model tether + no-fallback (security requirement)

Diego — high-level notes from product: we can support the customer but need to define constraints and trade-offs. Key points: 

1) Per-route no-fallback flag: implementable as a routing policy that denies fallback. Implications: if the pinned variant is degraded/unavailable we'll return controlled error (503 + remediation message) rather than failover. That must be agreed in contract.

2) Model variant pinning: supported at the config layer. However, variants can diverge in tokenizer behavior and OOM characteristics; we need a pre-deployment validation (sanity prompts, latency profiling, token delta check).

3) Observability: require enhanced tracing and token-level cost reporting for those routes and request-scoped audit logs (for SOC/audit).

4) Deployment cadence: recommend a canary within EU region first (10% traffic) but since customer demands no-fallback, canary must be in a separate workspace that does not share fallback policies — effectively a shadow route for validation.

Action items for product: I'll draft a minimal "no-fallback operational playbook" covering validation tests, required metrics, and expected failure semantics. Sending a doc shortly.

Karthik
VP Product

> Draft attached: no_fallback_MOP_v1.docx
From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-18T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: EU-only model tether + no-fallback (security requirement)

Diego / Karthik — ops feasibility notes:

- Runbook: will produce a separate MOP (deployment checklist) but top-level steps are: pre-deploy validation, deploy pinned variant to EU pool, enable per-route no-fallback flag, monitor KV cache warming and request latencies for 24h, then open to production. See attached checklist.
- Failure modes: if pinned model hits OOM or node failure, our behavior will be controlled 503 with clear retry guidance to the customer. We cannot silently reroute if no-fallback is enforced.
- Autoscaling: to reduce risk we recommend reserving capacity in the dedicated EU pool (reserved instances) during the pilot window — otherwise cold starts under pressure are higher risk.
- Time estimate: ~6 weeks end-to-end (1 week infra prep, 2 weeks product/config changes + testing, 2 weeks internal Canary + docs, 1 week legal/contracting).
- Contract: Ops needs the explicit SLA amendment: acceptable error modes, maintenance window allowances, and pre-agreed remediation credits. Please loop in sales/legal.

Marissa
SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachment: mop_deployment_checklist.xlsx
From: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-04-18T16:38:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Request: EU-only model tether + no-fallback (security requirement)

Olivia / Tom — thanks for the ask and for the questionnaire. Quick summary from our side:

- Redwood can support an EU-only, pinned-variant deployment with a per-route no-fallback policy.
- Operational implication: if the pinned variant becomes unavailable, Redwood will return a controlled error (503) and not failover to other variants. This behavior will be documented as part of the contract amendment (we will include explicit maintenance windows / remediation credits).
- Workstream & ETA: we estimate ~6 weeks to delivery as follows: infra reservation (EU dedicated pool), product config + validation, ops runbook + observability, and contract amendment.

Next steps I propose:
1) Review the attached draft playbook (we provided a first-pass MOP).
2) Approve the mutual action plan (link) so sales/legal can start the SOW/contract changes.
3) Schedule a 30-min technical review with your InfoSec next week to go over the questionnaire answers (CC: Tom).

I'll add a short summary to the HubSpot deal and track the action items. If you want us to accelerate the timeline we can look at prioritizing resources but that will need an updated commitment.

Diego
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
